title: Lighthouse Reef and the Great Blue Hole

briefing.summary: Survey Lighthouse Reef atoll in Belize: the shallow reef flat, its outer drop-off into open water, the reef life along the rim, and a marker at the real coordinates of the Great Blue Hole -- a famous 124 m sinkhole that this survey's bathymetry is too coarse to show.
facts: The Great Blue Hole is real and famous, but this open bathymetry has no dedicated high-resolution survey of it: at its published coordinates, this tile reads only a few metres deep, not the true 124 m sinkhole. The field guide explains what a proper 2018 sonar survey actually found there.
The reef flat around the hole is shallow, mostly under 10 m, then drops steeply to open ocean a few kilometres out -- both features are real, if coarse, survey terrain.
You start at the surface over the outer slope, in water well over 60 m deep. Head west (about 270°) toward the reef flat and the hole's marked position.
This is part of the Belize Barrier Reef Reserve System, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Keep a respectful distance from the reef.
hazards: Shallow reef structure near the rim -- watch your depth and avoid contact with coral.
A steep drop-off from the reef flat to open ocean; currents can be stronger there.
Total darkness below a few hundred metres on the outer slope; only your lights work.
Your Class A hull is rated to 1,000 m, comfortably beyond anything on this survey.

objectives.title: Find the Great Blue Hole's real coordinates
objectives.hint: The Great Blue Hole coordinate marker is on the shallow reef flat, around 4 m in this coarse tile; the real 124 m sinkhole is unresolved.

objectives.title: Survey the reef flat surrounding the hole
objectives.hint: Survey Lighthouse Reef's real, shallow reef flat northwest of the hole marker, only a few metres deep.

objectives.title: Follow the outer drop-off into open water
objectives.hint: The atoll's outer drop-off is east of the hole marker, where the mapped seabed falls to around 200 m.

objectives.title: Observe reef life along the rim
objectives.hint: The illustrative reef-life marker shares the shallow reef-flat area northwest of the hole; it is not a species sighting at this point.
